system.one_liner: An empirical study of diffusion planning in offline RL that lays out four design components and the choices compared for each.

content.variant_note: (a) a noise-to-plan denoising pipeline shown on a 3-joint robot arm; (b) a four-branch tree of design components with candidate boxes and red stars on the preferred ones
content.argues: A diffusion planner can be described by four design components, each with candidate choices, and the starred choices (jump-step planning, Transformer, inverse dynamics, sampling with selection) are the preferred ones.
content.subject: denoising noise into a robot-arm plan, and a four-branch tree of design choices with starred preferred options

lessons.what_to_learn: Lay out a design space as small trees with one colour per component, white option boxes outlined in that colour and a red star on the preferred choice, and repeat the component colours on the pipeline drawing beside it so each choice can be located.
lessons.suits: Empirical or design-space studies that compare several choices per component and want to mark the recommended configuration.

evidence: we begin by listing key design components (excluding common deep learning hyperparameters such as learning rates)
Each color corresponds to one component in the framework. A star indicates the preferred choice in experiments.

summary: The paper studies what makes a good diffusion planner for offline decision making. Figure 1(a) shows the framework: a grey Gaussian-noise grid goes through an orange Denoising Network, trained on a robot trajectory dataset (demonstrations), and becomes a trajectory plan grid over steps t to t+H-1, illustrated with a grey 3-joint robot arm and a strip of green arm poses. Figure 1(b) is a design space as four small trees, one colour per component: Planning Strategy, Denoising Network Backbone, Action Generation and Guided Sampling Algorithms, each with white option boxes and mini diagrams, and a red star on the preferred option: jump-step planning, Transformer, inverse dynamics and Monte Carlo sampling with selection.
